solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who takes issue for a while

definitions.text: One who takes issue for a while

parts.words: One who takes issue for a while
parts.note: issue here means offspring, so this is someone who takes in other people's children for part of the day

explanation.surface: A description of a quarrelsome person who picks arguments for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes issue' reads as disagreeing, but issue means children: the person minds them for a while, usually while parents work.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid carer looks after other people's young children for some hours, so the cryptic description fits exactly.

clue.text: Bird starts to collect eggs from here

parts.note: a hen is a bird

indicators.note: starts to says the first letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: A hen begins gathering its eggs from this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence is an old adverb meaning from this place, as in get thee hence.

clue.text: Rickety latticework, not fitting to a T in islands' capital

indicators.note: rickety means shaky, so the letters are shaken into a new order
not fitting says the letters of the following phrase are left out of the shuffle

explanation.surface: A tumbledown wooden lattice that does not fit precisely in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' shuffles LATTICEWORK, and 'not fitting' takes out the letters of 'to a T' (TOAT), leaving the answer's letters; 'to a T' looks like a phrase meaning exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerwick is the main town and capital of Shetland, a group of Scottish islands.

clue.text: Movement in Highland eisteddfod before 9

indicators.note: before says the festival comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: the Mod is the Gaelic festival of music and poetry in the Scottish Highlands, like the Welsh eisteddfod
the answer to 9 across is the Muse ERATO

explanation.surface: A musical piece played at a Scottish festival before a ninth item.
explanation.walkthrough: An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry; the Mod is its Scottish Gaelic counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is a tempo marking used as a title for a movement of a larger musical work.

clue.text: Marine environment needing much understanding

definitions.meaning: a profound idea is hard to grasp

explanation.surface: An ocean habitat that takes a lot of study to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic name for the sea, and deep also means profound and hard to fathom.

clue.text: Servicemen arm perhaps for recall …

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of servicemen
an arm is an example of a member, a limb

explanation.surface: Soldiers arming themselves in readiness for being called back.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next; 'arm' looks like a verb meaning to equip with weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: … serviceman who enjoys Macaulay?

parts.note: Macaulay wrote the Lays of Ancient Rome, so a fan reads lays; and a church service may be led by an unordained layperson

explanation.surface: A soldier who likes reading the historian Macaulay.
explanation.walkthrough: Serviceman means someone who takes church services, not a soldier; Thomas Macaulay's best-known poems are the Lays of Ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is an unordained person licensed to lead church services, and literally a reader of lays.

clue.text: Count to ten? 100 or 1000 is incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect says the letters as given are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

parts.note: to ten and or and is are taken as written, with C the Roman numeral for 100 and M for 1000

explanation.surface: A child counting to ten gets the hundred or thousand wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' is a title, not a verb; 'incorrect' shuffles TO TEN, C, OR, M and IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Count of Monte Cristo is the hero of the Dumas novel, the title character.

clue.text: Holy books are returned as source of inspiration

indicators.note: returned says the letters are read back to front

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the holy books of the first part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Sacred texts brought back as a source of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns OTARE round to read from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, and the Muses were the classical goddesses who inspired artists.

clue.text: Bring in reduction, as arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the word before are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An office instruction to bring in a cut, as agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals a shuffle of the letters of 'reduction'.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a new measure or product is to bring it in, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Seaside entertainer in his performance area? Tosh!

parts.note: a pier is where a seaside show is staged at a British resort
tosh means nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a seaside performer on his stage as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: British resorts have long piers with theatres at the end, where seaside shows were put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a white-faced clown figure who performed in traditional troupes at British seaside resorts.

clue.text: In a tizzy, gripe about daughter seen uncovered in family history

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the next piece
being in a tizzy is being flustered, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder
uncovered says the outer letters of the word are stripped away

explanation.surface: Someone flustered complains about a daughter being seen exposed in the family records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a tizzy' shuffles the gripe letters to PEIGR, which 'about' wraps round D; 'uncovered' removes the outer letters of 'seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a recorded line of ancestry, i.e. the lineage of a person or animal.

clue.text: After endless investigation, variation in climate is seen as tricky

indicators.note: endless says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a probe is an investigation

indicators.note: variation in says the letters of the following word are varied, rearranged

explanation.surface: An unfinished inquiry finds climate change hard to call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims PROBE to PROB; 'variation in' shuffles CLIMATE to LEMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something problematic is difficult to deal with, so it is a synonym of tricky.

clue.text: Late afternoon siesta — it's hard to get up

parts.note: eve, evening, follows the late afternoon
a siesta is an afternoon rest

explanation.surface: After an afternoon nap it is a struggle to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's hard to get up' looks like a remark about waking, but it describes a mountain that is difficult to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is notoriously difficult to climb, so it is hard to get up.

clue.text: Drink's cold after vehicle containing trendy bishop left

indicators.note: after says the cold piece comes at the end, following the rest
containing says the vehicle's word holds the following letters within it

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
in means fashionable, trendy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone's drink has gone cold after a fashionable bishop left the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts the trendy, bishop and left letters together inside the vehicle, making VINBLAN before the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin blanc is French for white wine, a drink.

clue.text: Expression that may come from pen unable to write?

definitions.text: Expression that may come from pen unable to write?

parts.words: Expression that may come from pen unable to write?
parts.note: the pen is a pigsty rather than a writing tool, so the sound is the grunt a pig makes from its enclosure

explanation.surface: Whatever might come from a pen that has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen means a pig's enclosure, and a pen unable to write has nothing, zero, in the way of writing fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a pig makes is the sound one hears from a sty, so it is an utterance from the pen.

clue.text: After a makeover, I enter fit for a queen

indicators.note: a makeover is a change of appearance, so the letters are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: A beauty makeover makes someone fit to be seen by royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After a makeover' shuffles the letters of 'I enter fit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the queen of ancient Egypt, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: Eating nothing is not so easy for a squirrel

indicators.note: eating says the first word swallows the next, holding it inside

parts.note: harder means not so easy
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A squirrel finds it tougher going when there is no food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squirrel' is used as a noun for a person who stores things away.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel, figuratively, is someone who stashes things away for later, which is just what a stockpiler does.

clue.text: Eminent graduate's second service

parts.note: high means eminent, of great rank
MA is a Master of Arts graduate, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A distinguished graduate's second time at church.
explanation.definitionFit: High Mass is a Roman Catholic church service with full ceremony and music.

clue.text: College waiter upset me first

indicators.note: first says the overturned piece comes at the front
upset in a down clue says the letters are turned over, read bottom to top

parts.note: Manuel is the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: A college waiter is upset that he put me first.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a 1970s British TV comedy set in a hotel; its hapless waiter is Manuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is one of the colleges of Cambridge University.

clue.text: Minerals located in the heart of Arden, say

indicators.note: the heart of says only the middle of the word is kept, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is an example of a forest, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Minerals found deep in the Arden countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arden' does not give letters itself: it stands for FOREST, and 'the heart of' drops its first and last letters, F and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ores are natural rocks or minerals from which metals are extracted.

clue.text: Address of worn-out runner?

parts.note: old means worn-out
a runner bean is a climbing bean grown in British gardens

explanation.surface: The speech of an exhausted athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' is a form of address, a term used to greet someone; 'runner' looks like an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is a dated, upper-class British term of address, like old chap.

clue.text: Record Greens organising decorations for board?

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: organising says the letters of the following word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The Greens are planning decorations for a council board meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Board here means a dining table; 'organising' shuffles GREENS to ERGNES.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, so it decorates the board in its old sense of table.

clue.text: How to read a palindrome whilst watching the pendulum?

definitions.text: How to read a palindrome whilst watching the pendulum?

parts.words: How to read a palindrome whilst watching the pendulum?
parts.note: a palindrome reads the same either way, and a pendulum swings one way then back

explanation.surface: A puzzle about reading a symmetrical word while staring at a swinging clock weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe motion back and forth: reading forwards then backwards, and the swing of a pendulum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means moving backwards and forwards, which fits both the swing and the two-way reading.

clue.text: Formal procedures necessary to inherit estate

indicators.note: necessary to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Legal formalities required before taking over a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are ceremonies, set formal procedures, especially religious ones.

clue.text: Now and then in American square?

parts.note: in and at both give a location, as in at home
Times Square is a famous square in New York

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally found in an American town square.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, from time to time, which is a synonym of now and then.

clue.text: Half the wine? Half it is!

indicators.note: Half says only the first half of the word's letters are kept

parts.note: Semillon is a white wine grape, and wine made from it

explanation.surface: Someone asks if half the wine is gone and is told it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The prefix means half, so the last words define it.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix semi- means half, as in semicircle.

clue.text: Tee up late when playing for decoration

indicators.note: when playing hints at golf play, here meaning the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A golfer tees up late while in the middle of a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when playing' shuffles the letters of 'Tee up late'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is an ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform, a decoration of rank.

clue.text: One cut out sugar at first to get fit

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: out says the letters of the word are disordered
at first says only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out sugar first to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like 'in good shape', but here it is a noun, a seizure; 'out' shuffles CUT to CTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ictus is a medical term for a seizure or stroke, the same as a sudden fit.

clue.text: Good behaviour isn't commonly linked with rows on board

indicators.note: on, with board, says the other letters sit inside the ship's letters

parts.note: on board is the convention for inside a ship, SS, a steamship
ain't is the common, non-standard form of isn't
rows are lines

explanation.surface: Good behaviour on a ship means not mixing with the rowing crews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't commonly' is the dialect form ain't; 'on board' is the convention for sitting inside a steamship's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being saintly means behaving very well, so holiness of conduct is good behaviour.
